title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk
book_title: The KPI Dashboard & Sponsor Accountability: Tracking Error, Liquidity, and Walk-the-Talk

epigraph.quote: A leveraged ETF sponsor cannot control the index, but it is 100% accountable for daily tracking precision, counterparty diversification, and fee discipline.
epigraph.author: ETF Governance & Fiduciary Standard

web_blocks.html: Evaluating operational quality for KORU requires a specialized framework [1][2]. A 3x daily synthetic ETF differs fundamentally from an industrial manufacturer or software enterprise [1]. Rafferty Asset Management does not manufacture memory chips or set Korean monetary policy [1]. Instead, fund operational execution is evaluated across five objective metrics [1][6]. These include Daily Leverage Precision, targeting ~300% gross exposure at each 4:00 PM ET close [1]. They also encompass Swap Financing Spreads and Counterparty Breadth across prime brokers [1]. The remaining three metrics are Collateral Yield Offset, AUM and Secondary Liquidity Scale, and Portfolio Turnover Discipline [1][6].

web_blocks.explanatory_p: 1H FY2026 filings shift two formerly passing KPIs onto Watch: portfolio turnover surged to 264% in six months, and Citibank's swap spread doubled to SOFR+1.70% while collateral yields slipped below SOFR [8][10].
web_blocks.takeaway: KPI Health is PASS_WITH_WATCH: Rafferty executes daily resets across seven Tier-1 swap dealers, but 264% turnover and SOFR+170 bps spreads require close monitoring [8][9].

web_blocks.html: On Structural Potential, KORU's upside and downside drivers depend on two structural pillars inside the MSCI Korea 25/50 Index [4]. The first pillar is South Korea's AI and High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) duopoly [4]. SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics represent approximately 42%–48% of the total index [4]. Global cloud hyperscalers continue expanding capital expenditures into HBM3e, HBM4, and DDR5 enterprise servers [4]. This commercial shift drives high operating leverage and multi-quarter earnings revisions across Seoul [4]. Persistent daily upward trends create an ideal operating environment for 3x daily compounding [1][4]. The second pillar is South Korea's Corporate Value-Up Program [4]. This regulatory effort aims to narrow the persistent valuation discount applied to Korean equities [4]. It incentivizes chaebol affiliates, commercial banks, and industrial leaders to retire treasury shares [4]. It also encourages higher dividend payout ratios and improved return on equity [4].

At the same time, an institutional audit must account for three structural caps and regulatory-FX risks [4][8][10]. First, the MSCI 25/50 capping rule trims top issuers toward 25%, yet Information Technology still reached 50.1% of the index on April 30, 2026 (alongside 22.1% Industrials) [8]. That 72.2% tech-plus-industrial export concentration leaves KORU acutely exposed to U.S. semiconductor export controls and tariff shifts [8][12]. Second, Korean Won (KRW) FX volatility compounds equity shocks inside USD-denominated EWY swaps [1][10]. Per Federal Reserve H.10 data (FRED DEXKOUS), the Won traded at 1,336.58 KRW/USD on November 13, 2026 after weakening to 1,361.89 on November 6, 2026 [10]. Third, negative rate carry tightened fund economics: collateral yields slipped to 3.52%–3.55% in April 2026 against 3.91% SOFR in November 2026 [8][10].

web_blocks.title: Sponsor Walk-the-Talk Audit: Rafferty Asset Management, LLC
paragraphs: 1. Fee Cap & Breakpoint Integrity. Rafferty capped operating expenses at 0.95% through September 1, 2026 [1][8]. When net assets briefly crossed $1.55 billion on April 30, 2026, the $1.5B advisory breakpoint triggered a $2,071 fee waiver, while annualized ex-interest net expenses fell to 0.90% (0.89% pre-recoupment) [8]. On October 27, 2026, Direxion filed an updated Advisory Fee Waiver Agreement extending the tiered 0.75%–0.55% breakpoint schedule through September 1, 2028 [13].

2. Candid Risk Disclosure. Direxion avoids marketing KORU as a long-term compounder [1][2]. Form N-CSR and the statutory prospectus explicitly warn that annual returns should not suggest long-term holding suitability [1][2]. The sponsor prominently discloses that daily compounding causes multi-day returns to diverge sharply from 3x benchmark returns [1][2].

3. Scale Breakpoints. KORU proved its breakpoint mechanics work by waiving $2,071 when assets passed $1.55 billion in April 2026 [8]. However, with AUM moderating to $747.35 million in November 2026, the fund currently pays the full 0.75% base advisory tier [6][13].

web_blocks.html: Looking ahead, the single most informative operational KPI is the spread between realized 30-day EWY volatility and directional drift [5]. This metric matters even more than underlying DRAM spot pricing [5]. When EWY annualized volatility holds below ~25% during an upward trend, 3x daily resets add positive compounding momentum [5]. Conversely, when realized volatility exceeds ~40% in a choppy market, quadratic variance drag overwhelms underlying equity gains [5]. Monitoring collateral yield against swap spreads provides a second operational indicator [1]. By April 30, 2026, money market collateral yielded 3.52%–3.55% against 3.91% SOFR plus 70 to 170 basis points in swap spreads [8][10]. Tracking that gap reveals negative net synthetic carry [8][10].

book_paragraphs: When you evaluate an ordinary operating company, you track same-store sales, gross margins, and customer churn. When you evaluate KORU, you have to build a completely different operational dashboard. You are auditing whether Rafferty Asset Management is running a tight, low-friction derivatives machine—and whether the underlying Korean market structure supports the kind of trending regime where 3x daily leverage works.

Look at how those operational KPIs evolved in the April 30, 2026 semi-annual report and July 31, 2026 Form NPORT-P. Effective exposure stayed tight at 300.0% in April and 287.0% gross in July, and Rafferty expanded its dealer roster from four banks to seven by adding BNP Paribas, UBS, and Nomura. However, Citibank doubled its swap spread to SOFR plus 170 basis points, and BNP Paribas and UBS entered at SOFR plus 95 and 90 basis points—lifting funding costs sharply above the 2025 baseline.

At the same time, collateral yields slipped to 3.52%–3.55% against a 3.91% SOFR rate, cutting annualized net investment income from 1.85% in FY2025 to 0.84% in 1H FY2026. Worse, physical EWY portfolio turnover jumped from 81% to 264% in just six months amid $1.8 billion in combined creation and redemption flows. Operational execution still earns PASS_WITH_WATCH, but swap spread inflation, 264% turnover, and Korean Won swings between 1,336 and 1,362 per dollar require active monitoring.

On sponsor walk-the-talk, Rafferty deserves credit for honoring its $1.5 billion fee breakpoint in April 2026, waiving $2,071 in advisory fees as annualized ex-interest expenses dropped to 0.90%, and extending its tiered fee waiver schedule through September 1, 2028. And with Information Technology alone representing 50.1% of the index—plus Industrials at 22.1%—any trader using KORU must watch U.S. semiconductor tariff policy and KRW/USD stability just as closely as DRAM pricing.

If you want to monitor KORU's structural potential going forward without getting lost in daily noise, watch two underlying Korean catalysts and one mathematical gauge. The first catalyst is High-Bandwidth Memory capacity and pricing at SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, which together drive nearly half of the capped index's weight. The second is Seoul's Corporate Value-Up Program—specifically whether Korean banks, holding companies, and automakers follow through on share cancellations and higher payout ratios that can lift Korea's depressed price-to-book multiples.

The mathematical gauge is the tug-of-war between realized volatility and trend persistence. When South Korean equities trend steadily upward with 20% to 25% annualized volatility, KORU's daily reset compounds in your favor. The moment realized volatility spikes past 40% in a choppy, headline-driven tape—whether from tariff threats, Won swings, or semiconductor inventory scares—variance drag takes over the driver's seat regardless of how cheap Korean stocks look on paper.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good governance in a leveraged ETF does not mean protecting investors from drawdowns—no sponsor can repeal 3x beta or variance math. It means keeping swap spreads tight, diversifying counterparties across seven Tier-1 banks, honoring the 0.95% operating cap, and telling the truth in plain English about single-day design. On those criteria, Rafferty walks the talk.

section_takeaway: KPI Health stays PASS_WITH_WATCH as 7-dealer breadth and $1.5B breakpoint execution offset 2026 watches: 264% 6-month turnover, Citibank SOFR+170 bps swap spreads, 50.1% IT weight, and 1,337–1,362 KRW/USD FX risk [8][9][10].
